title: QuickBooks vs Dolibarr
comparison_markdown:
# QuickBooks vs Dolibarr (2026)

## Overview
QuickBooks and Dolibarr are both accounting and management tools designed to help businesses and organizations manage their finances, inventory, and operations. This comparison is beneficial for small to medium-sized businesses, freelancers, and non-profit organizations looking for a cost-effective and customizable solution. The core use case for both tools is to streamline financial management, and a key reason someone would switch is to gain more control over their data and reduce costs.

## Key Differences
* Cost: QuickBooks offers a range of pricing plans, while Dolibarr is free and open-source.
* Data ownership: With Dolibarr, users have full ownership and control over their data, whereas QuickBooks stores data on its servers.
* Setup complexity: QuickBooks has a more user-friendly setup process, while Dolibarr requires more technical expertise.
* Scalability: Dolibarr is highly scalable and can be customized to meet the needs of growing businesses, whereas QuickBooks has limitations on the number of users and features.
* Feature difference: Dolibarr offers a built-in CRM module, while QuickBooks requires a separate subscription for its CRM features.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | QuickBooks | Dolibarr |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $30-$200+/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | GPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $1,500-$6,000+/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $6,000-$24,000+/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**QuickBooks:**
* User-friendly interface
* Wide range of integrations with other tools
* Good customer support
* Scalable plans for growing businesses
* Limited customization options
**Dolibarr:**
* Free and open-source
* High customization options
* Scalable and flexible
* Built-in CRM module
* Steeper learning curve due to technical requirements

## When to Choose Each
QuickBooks is a good choice for small to medium-sized businesses that need a user-friendly and straightforward accounting solution. It's ideal for teams with limited technical expertise and a focus on ease of use. On the other hand, Dolibarr is suitable for businesses that require a high degree of customization, data ownership, and scalability. It's ideal for teams with technical expertise and a focus on flexibility and control.

## Migration Path
1. Export data from QuickBooks in CSV or Excel format.
2. Install and configure Dolibarr on a self-hosted server.
3. Use the Dolibarr import tool to migrate data from QuickBooks.
4. Configure and customize Dolibarr to meet specific business needs.
5. Test and verify the migration to ensure data integrity and accuracy.

## Our Take
Dolibarr is not yet production-ready for most users due to its technical requirements and steep learning curve. However, for businesses with technical expertise, Dolibarr offers a high degree of customization and flexibility. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that Dolibarr requires a good understanding of server management and configuration. We recommend switching to Dolibarr for businesses that require a high degree of customization and control over their data, but not for those who prioritize ease of use and a user-friendly interface.

## Who Should Switch
* Small businesses with technical expertise and a focus on customization
* Non-profit organizations with limited budgets and a need for free and open-source solutions
* Freelancers who require a high degree of flexibility and control over their finances
* Businesses with 10-50 users who do not need advanced CRM features
* Teams with existing self-hosted infrastructure and a focus on data ownership

## FAQ
### Is Dolibarr free?
Yes, Dolibarr is free and open-source, with no costs or licensing fees.
### Can I self-host Dolibarr?
Yes, Dolibarr can be self-hosted on a server, giving users full control over their data and configuration.
### Is QuickBooks scalable?
Yes, QuickBooks offers scalable plans for growing businesses, but with limitations on the number of users and features.
### Does Dolibarr have a built-in CRM module?
Yes, Dolibarr has a built-in CRM module, whereas QuickBooks requires a separate subscription for its CRM features.
### Can I migrate data from QuickBooks to Dolibarr?
Yes, data can be exported from QuickBooks in CSV or Excel format and imported into Dolibarr using its import tool.

title: Zoho CRM vs Dolibarr

# Zoho CRM vs Dolibarr (2026)

## Overview
Zoho CRM and Dolibarr are both customer relationship management tools designed to help businesses manage their sales, marketing, and customer service activities. This comparison is beneficial for small to medium-sized businesses looking to switch from a proprietary CRM to a self-hosted, open-source alternative. The core use case for both tools is to streamline customer interactions and improve sales performance, with the key reason to switch being the desire for greater control over data and costs.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Zoho CRM has a monthly subscription fee, while Dolibarr is free to use and self-host.
* Data ownership: Zoho CRM stores data on its proprietary servers, whereas Dolibarr allows users to host their data on their own servers.
* Setup complexity: Zoho CRM has a more streamlined setup process, while Dolibarr requires more technical expertise to set up and configure.
* Scalability: Zoho CRM has built-in scalability features, while Dolibarr's scalability depends on the user's server infrastructure.
* Integration with Google Drive: Zoho CRM has native integration with Google Drive, while Dolibarr requires a third-party module for similar functionality.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Zoho CRM | Dolibarr |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $14-$52/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | GPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $700-$2,600/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $2,800-$10,400/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
### Zoho CRM
* Pros:
	+ User-friendly interface
	+ Robust sales and marketing automation features
	+ Native integration with Google Drive
	+ Scalable and reliable infrastructure
	+ 24/7 customer support
* Cons:
	+ Monthly subscription fees can add up
	+ Limited customization options
	+ Data stored on proprietary servers
	+ Limited control over data and security
### Dolibarr
* Pros:
	+ Free to use and self-host
	+ Open-source and customizable
	+ Data stored on user's own servers
	+ Modular design for flexibility
	+ Active community support
* Cons:
	+ Steeper learning curve
	+ Requires technical expertise for setup and configuration
	+ Limited native integration with third-party tools
	+ Dependence on user's server infrastructure for scalability
	+ Limited 24/7 customer support

## When to Choose Each
Zoho CRM is suitable for businesses that prioritize ease of use, scalability, and 24/7 customer support. It is ideal for large teams with complex sales and marketing operations who can afford the monthly subscription fees. On the other hand, Dolibarr is suitable for small to medium-sized businesses that value control over their data, customization options, and cost-effectiveness. It is ideal for teams with technical expertise who can handle the setup and configuration process.

## Migration Path
1. Export data from Zoho CRM in CSV format.
2. Install and configure Dolibarr on the user's server.
3. Use the Dolibarr import tool to import the CSV data.
4. Configure and customize Dolibarr to meet the user's specific needs.
5. Test and verify the migrated data and functionality.

## Our Take
Dolibarr is not yet production-ready for most users due to its steep learning curve and limited native integration with third-party tools. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that Dolibarr's scalability depends on the user's server infrastructure, which can be a challenge for large teams. However, for small to medium-sized businesses with technical expertise, Dolibarr is a viable alternative to Zoho CRM, offering greater control over data and costs.

## Who Should Switch
* Small businesses with fewer than 10 users who do not need advanced sales and marketing automation features.
* Teams with technical expertise who can handle the setup and configuration process.
* Businesses that prioritize data ownership and control over ease of use.
* Companies with limited budgets who cannot afford monthly subscription fees.
* Organizations that require customization options and modular design.

## FAQ
### Is Dolibarr free to use?
Yes, Dolibarr is free to use and self-host.
### Can I integrate Dolibarr with Google Drive?
Yes, but it requires a third-party module.
### Is Zoho CRM scalable?
Yes, Zoho CRM has built-in scalability features.
### Can I customize Dolibarr to meet my specific needs?
Yes, Dolibarr is open-source and customizable.
### Is Dolibarr suitable for large teams?
Not yet, due to its limited native integration with third-party tools and dependence on user's server infrastructure for scalability.

title: Salesforce vs Dolibarr

# Salesforce vs Dolibarr

## Overview

Salesforce is the enterprise CRM standard, powerful but expensive and complex. Dolibarr is a free open-source ERP and CRM built for SMBs, covering customer management, invoicing, stock, and projects in one self-hosted package — at a fraction of the operational cost.

## Key Differences

- **Cost**: Salesforce costs $25-$300+/user/month; Dolibarr is free with server costs under $15/month
- **Target scale**: Salesforce is built for large enterprises; Dolibarr is optimized for SMBs under 100 users
- **ERP scope**: Dolibarr combines CRM with accounting and inventory; Salesforce requires expensive add-ons for that
- **Implementation**: Salesforce typically needs a consultant to implement; Dolibarr can be set up by a non-specialist
- **Data ownership**: Dolibarr self-hosted gives you full control; Salesforce data lives on their infrastructure

## Pricing Comparison

| Aspect | Salesforce | Dolibarr |
|--------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Base pricing | $25-$300+/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | GPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Cost at 50 users | ~$1,250/month | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Cost at 200 users | ~$5,000/month | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Vendor lock-in | High | None |

## Pros and Cons

### Salesforce

**Pros:**
- Polished, professionally designed user interface
- Large ecosystem of official integrations
- Managed infrastructure with no server maintenance required
- Enterprise SLA and dedicated support available
- Mobile apps are well-maintained and reliable

**Cons:**
- Significant per-user monthly cost that scales linearly with team size
- Your data is stored on the vendor infrastructure
- No ability to inspect or modify the source code
- Feature roadmap controlled entirely by the vendor
- Risk of pricing changes, acquisition, or discontinuation

### Dolibarr

**Pros:**
- Free to self-host with costs only for server infrastructure
- Complete data ownership and privacy control
- Source code is auditable and modifiable
- Active open-source community
- No vendor lock-in or risk of sudden pricing changes
> GitHub: [Dolibarr/dolibarr](https://github.com/Dolibarr/dolibarr) * ~5k stars

**Cons:**
- Requires technical knowledge to self-host and maintain
- May lack some advanced features found in the proprietary version
- Support relies on community forums rather than a paid helpdesk
- UI polish may lag behind the proprietary tool
- You are responsible for updates, backups, and security patches

## When to Choose Each

**Choose Salesforce if:** Salesforce suits enterprises with dedicated CRM admin teams, complex multi-territory sales operations, and budgets that justify $1,000-$10,000+/month in licenses.

**Choose Dolibarr if:** Dolibarr is ideal for SMBs that were pushed toward Salesforce by a consultant but actually only need basic pipeline tracking, invoicing, and contact management.

## Migration Path

Use Salesforce Data Export Service to download CSVs of Accounts, Contacts, Opportunities, and Tasks. Import Accounts and Contacts into Dolibarr's Third Parties module, and Opportunities into the Projects or CRM Opportunities module. Recreate key Salesforce reports manually as Dolibarr report templates.

## Our Take

Dolibarr is production-ready for most teams willing to invest a few hours in setup. The self-hosted version gives you identical or better functionality to the paid Salesforce tiers, with no recurring per-seat cost.

The main technical limitation worth knowing: you are responsible for your own backups, updates, and uptime. If your server goes down, so does your Dolibarr instance. Plan for this with automated backups and a monitoring alert.

Our recommendation: if your team has at least one developer and you are paying more than $100/month for Salesforce, switching to self-hosted Dolibarr will pay for itself within the first month. If nobody on your team is comfortable with Linux or Docker, stay on Salesforce until you have that resource.

## Who Should Switch

- Startups under 20 people paying per-seat fees they cannot yet justify
- Dev teams who already self-host other tools and have the ops knowledge
- Organizations in jurisdictions with strict data residency requirements
- Teams who have evaluated Salesforce paid features and only use the basics
- Founders and solopreneurs who want the functionality without the subscription

## FAQ

### Is Dolibarr free to use?
Yes. Dolibarr is free to self-host. Your only cost is the server, typically $6-$12/month on a VPS provider like DigitalOcean or Vultr.

### How hard is it to migrate from Salesforce to Dolibarr?
For most teams, migration takes 2-4 hours. Export your Salesforce data, follow the Dolibarr import guide, and test with a small group before switching everyone over.

### Does Dolibarr get regular updates?
Yes. Dolibarr has an active open-source community with regular releases. Check the GitHub repository for release frequency.

### Can I use Dolibarr without technical knowledge?
You need basic comfort with a VPS and command line. If that feels unfamiliar, there are managed hosting options that handle the server for you at a modest cost.

### What happens if Dolibarr development stops?
Because the source code is open, you can continue running whatever version you have indefinitely. You can also fork the project or switch to another tool at your own pace — no vendor can shut off your instance.

---
*Data sourced July 2026. Pricing and features change. Verify at [Salesforce](https://salesforce.com) and [Dolibarr](https://dolibarr.org) before making decisions.*
